finding.text: `compact_after: null` on the `ai-system-mastermind` row (`Servex/agents/roles.js:53`) also turns off the 400k safety ceiling, because `Agent.oversized()` returns null for any role with `compact_after === null` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:1515`). That contradicts the row's own comment ("only the 400k safety ceiling applies mid-work"). Renewal only happens on a wake from dormant, so a session that keeps itself awake with timers (its readme's "Don't fall asleep with work in flight") is never renewed and never compacted, and it grows toward the 1M window. Fix: keep the ceiling for this role, e.g. `compact_after: { tokens: Infinity }` or an `oversized()` check that skips only nudges for `renew` roles, plus one test.

A singleton spawn looks only at `this.live` (`Agents.js:134`). After a Servex restart, a young session that exists only in the registry gets a brand-new session under the same id instead of being resumed, which loses its context for no reason. `Agents.wake()` already handles a registry-only agent; the singleton branch could route there when a registry row exists.

Changing the generic `mastermind` row's readme from `servex-mastermind` to `mastermind` (`roles.js:55`) changes the system prompt of every live Servex-spawned mastermind (e.g. a deputy) on its next resume. It is probably right, but nobody asked for it; it is recorded in requirements.md, so just check that the deputy's role still fits.

`Server/on-landing.mjs:23-24` still sends landing check failures to a `servex-mastermind` task folder, not to the new feedback inbox (`module_inbox`, module `ai`). The landing checks are the main source of "problem + fix" lines, so pointing them at the inbox would let the third-repeat wake actually fire.

`Server/role-spend.mjs` is good, simple code. Its `ALIASES` (line 31) is a second list of old ids next to `roles.js`. The second review accepted that; it is noted here only so the two get updated together.
